Diatoms (chrysophytes) are microscopic, photosynthetic planktonic organisms with siliceous cell walls (frustules). They contribute a major portion of global oceanic primary production and are known as the chief producers in the oceans.

डायटम (क्राइसोफाइट) सिलिकामय कोशिका भित्ति (frustules) वाले सूक्ष्म, प्रकाश-संश्लेषी प्लवक जीव हैं। वे वैश्विक महासागरीय प्राथमिक उत्पादन में एक बड़े हिस्से का योगदान करते हैं और महासागरों में मुख्य उत्पादक के रूप में जाने जाते हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q153 - Population interaction used for antibiotics production is amensalism

questiontext.text:
Which one of the following population interactions is widely used in medical science for the production of antibiotics ?

चिकित्सा विज्ञान में एंटीबायोटिक दवाओं (प्रतिजैविकों) के उत्पादन के लिए निम्नलिखित में से किस समष्टि अंतःक्रिया का व्यापक रूप से उपयोग किया जाता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Amensalism is a population interaction in which one species is inhibited or harmed while the other species remains unaffected (\(-\), \(0\)). Antibiosis, such as the secretion of penicillin by Penicillium fungi to inhibit bacterial growth without being affected itself, is a form of amensalism widely exploited in medicine for antibiotic production.

एमेंसलिज्म (Amensalism) एक ऐसी समष्टि अंतःक्रिया है जिसमें एक प्रजाति को नुकसान या विरोध होता है जबकि दूसरी प्रजाति अप्रभावित रहती है (\(-\), \(0\))। एंटीबायोसिस, जैसे Penicillium कवक द्वारा पेनिसिलिन का स्राव जो कवक को स्वयं प्रभावित किए बिना जीवाणु वृद्धि को रोकता है, एमेंसलिज्म का एक रूप है जिसका उपयोग चिकित्सा में प्रतिजैविक उत्पादन के लिए किया जाता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q154 - Sacred groves are not ex-situ conservation

questiontext.text:
All of the following are included in 'Ex-situ conservation' except

निम्नलिखित में से किसे छोड़कर सभी 'बायो-स्थाने/उत्-स्थाने संरक्षण' (Ex-situ conservation) में शामिल हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Sacred groves are forest patches protected through traditional cultural and religious beliefs; they represent in-situ conservation (conservation of species within their natural habitats). Botanical gardens, wildlife safari parks, and seed banks are ex-situ conservation methods where threatened plants and animals are taken out of their natural habitat and placed in special care settings.

पवित्र उपवन (Sacred groves) पारंपरिक सांस्कृतिक और धार्मिक मान्यताओं द्वारा संरक्षित वन क्षेत्र हैं; वे स्व-स्थाने संरक्षण (In-situ conservation) का प्रतिनिधित्व करते हैं। वनस्पति उद्यान, वन्यजीव सफारी पार्क, और बीज बैंक उत्-स्थाने संरक्षण (Ex-situ conservation) की विधियां हैं जहाँ संकटग्रस्त जीवों को उनके प्राकृतिक आवास से बाहर निकालकर विशेष देखभाल में रखा जाता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MATCHING_MCQ_Q155 - Match environmental issues in Column I with Column II

questiontext.text:
Match the items given in Column I with those in Column II and select the correct option given below :

Column I Column II
a. Eutrophication i. UV-B radiation
b. Sanitary landfill ii. Deforestation
c. Snow blindness iii. Nutrient enrichment
d. Jhum cultivation iv. Waste disposal

कॉलम I में दी गई वस्तुओं का कॉलम II से मिलान कीजिए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए :

कॉलम I कॉलम II
a. सुपोषण (Eutrophication) i. UV-B विकिरण
b. सैनिटरी लैंडफिल ii. वनोन्मूलन (Deforestation)
c. हिम अंधता (Snow blindness) iii. पोषक संवर्धन (Nutrient enrichment)
d. झूम खेती (Jhum cultivation) iv. अपशिष्ट निपटान (Waste disposal)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Match Eutrophication.
Eutrophication is the natural or accelerated aging of a water body caused by nutrient enrichment (nitrates and phosphates).

Step 2: Match Sanitary Landfill.
Sanitary landfills are adopted as a method for solid waste disposal substituting open-burning dumps.

Step 3: Match Snow Blindness.
High doses of UV-B radiation cause inflammation of the cornea, commonly termed snow blindness cataract.

Step 4: Match Jhum Cultivation.
Jhum cultivation (slash and burn agriculture) practiced in north-eastern states of India has contributed significantly to deforestation.

Conclusion:
Matching each phenomenon with its cause/method yields a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

चरण 1: सुपोषण (Eutrophication) का मिलान करें।
सुपोषण जल निकाय का प्राकृतिक या त्वरित बुढ़ापा है जो पोषक संवर्धन (नाइट्रेट्स और फॉस्फेट्स) के कारण होता है।

चरण 2: सैनिटरी लैंडफिल का मिलान करें।
सैनिटरी लैंडफिल खुले में जलाने के स्थान पर ठोस अपशिष्ट निपटान की एक विधि के रूप में अपनाए जाते हैं।

चरण 3: हिम अंधता (Snow blindness) का मिलान करें।
UV-B विकिरण की उच्च खुराक से कॉर्निया का शोथ होता है, जिसे सामान्यतः हिम अंधता मोतियाबिंद कहा जाता है।

चरण 4: झूम खेती (Jhum cultivation) का मिलान करें।
भारत के पूर्वोत्तर राज्यों में की जाने वाली झूम खेती (काटो और जलाओ कृषि) ने वनोन्मूलन (Deforestation) में महत्वपूर्ण योगदान दिया है।

निष्कर्ष:
प्रत्येक परिघटना का उसके कारण/विधि से मिलान करने पर a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii प्राप्त होता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q156 - Growing population has more pre-reproductive individuals

questiontext.text:
In a growing population of a country,

किसी देश की बढ़ती (growing) समष्टि में,

generalfeedback.text:
A growing (expanding) population is characterized by a triangular age pyramid where the base representing pre-reproductive individuals is broader than the middle tier representing reproductive individuals. This ensures that a greater number of individuals will enter the reproductive age group in subsequent years.

एक बढ़ती (विस्तारित) समष्टि को त्रिकोणीय आयु पिरामिड द्वारा दर्शाया जाता है जहाँ जनन-पूर्व (pre-reproductive) व्यष्टियों को निरूपित करने वाला आधार जननक्षम (reproductive) व्यष्टियों को दर्शाने वाले मध्य स्तर से अधिक चौड़ा होता है। यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि आने वाले वर्षों में अधिक संख्या में व्यष्टि जनन आयु वर्ग में प्रवेश करेंगे।

answer.text: reproductive and pre-reproductive individuals are equal in number.
reproductive individuals are less than the post-reproductive individuals.
pre-reproductive individuals are more than the reproductive individuals.
pre-reproductive individuals are less than the reproductive individuals.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q157 - Drug Smack obtained from latex of poppy plant

questiontext.text:
Which part of poppy plant is used to obtain the drug "Smack" ?

ड्रग "स्मैक" (Smack) प्राप्त करने के लिए पोस्त (poppy) के पौधे के किस भाग का उपयोग किया जाता है?

generalfeedback.text:
"Smack" (heroin or diacetylmorphine) is chemically synthesized by the acetylation of morphine. Morphine is extracted directly from the dried milky latex harvested from the unripened capsules of the poppy plant (Papaver somniferum).

"स्मैक" (हीरोइन या डायसिटाइलमॉर्फिन) रासायनिक रूप से मॉर्फिन के एसिटिलीकरण द्वारा संश्लेषित किया जाता है। मॉर्फिन पोस्त के पौधे (Papaver somniferum) के अधपके कैप्सूल से निकाले गए सूखे दुधिया लेटेक्स से सीधे निकाला जाता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q158 - Enhancer is not part of operon

questiontext.text:
All of the following are part of an operon except

निम्नलिखित में से किसे छोड़कर सभी ओपेरॉन (operon) का हिस्सा हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
A prokaryotic operon is a polycistronic genetic unit comprising promoter sequence, operator region, regulator gene, and structural genes that function together under a unified control mechanism. Enhancers are eukaryotic cis-acting regulatory DNA sequences that increase transcription rate and are not part of prokaryotic operons.

एक प्रोकैरियोटिक ओपेरॉन एक पॉलिसिस्ट्रॉनिक आनुवंशिक इकाई है जिसमें प्रमोटर अनुक्रम, ऑपरेटर क्षेत्र, नियामक जीन, और संरचनात्मक जीन शामिल होते हैं जो एक एकीकृत नियंत्रण तंत्र के तहत एक साथ कार्य करते हैं। एन्हांसर (वर्धक) यूकैरियोटिक डीएनए अनुक्रम हैं जो प्रतिलेखन दर को बढ़ाते हैं और प्रोकैरियोटिक ओपेरॉन का हिस्सा नहीं हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q159 - X-linked condition inherited by both sons and daughters

questiontext.text:
A woman has an X-linked condition on one of her X chromosomes. This chromosome can be inherited by

एक महिला के अपने X गुणसूत्रों में से एक पर एक X-सहलग्न स्थिति (X-linked condition) है। यह गुणसूत्र किसके द्वारा वंशानुगत हो सकता है?

generalfeedback.text:
A mother transmits one of her two X chromosomes to every child regardless of sex. Male offspring receive their single X chromosome from the mother and Y from the father, while female offspring receive one X chromosome from the mother and one X from the father. Thus, both sons and daughters have a 50% probability of inheriting an X-linked allele carried by the mother.

एक माता लिंग की परवाह किए बिना प्रत्येक बच्चे को अपने दो X गुणसूत्रों में से एक संचारित करती है। पुत्रों को अपनी माता से एकल X गुणसूत्र और पिता से Y प्राप्त होता है, जबकि पुत्रियों को माता से एक X और पिता से एक X प्राप्त होता है। इस प्रकार, पुत्रों और पुत्रियों दोनों को माता द्वारा वहन किए जाने वाले X-सहलग्न एलील को वंशानुगत प्राप्त करने की 50% संभावना होती है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q160 - Hugo de Vries proposed saltation as mechanism of evolution

questiontext.text:
According to Hugo de Vries, the mechanism of evolution is

ह्यूगो डी ब्रीज के अनुसार, विकास (evolution) का तंत्र क्या है?

generalfeedback.text:
Hugo de Vries put forward the Mutation Theory of evolution based on his work on the evening primrose (Oenothera lamarckiana). He proposed that speciation occurs due to large, sudden, single-step random mutations, which he termed saltation, rather than small continuous variations proposed by Darwin.

ह्यूगो डी ब्रीज ने इवनिंग प्रिमरोज (Oenothera lamarckiana) पर अपने काम के आधार पर विकास का उत्परिवर्तन सिद्धांत प्रस्तुत किया। उन्होंने प्रस्तावित किया कि नई जातियों की उत्पत्ति डार्विन द्वारा प्रस्तावित छोटे निरंतर परिवर्तनों के बजाय बड़े, आकस्मिक, एकल-चरण यादृच्छिक उत्परिवर्तनों के कारण होती है, जिसे उन्होंने साल्टेशन (saltation) कहा।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q161 - Transcribed mRNA sequence from DNA coding strand

questiontext.text:
AGGTATCGCAT is a sequence from the coding strand of a gene. What will be the corresponding sequence of the transcribed mRNA ?

AGGTATCGCAT किसी जीन के कोडिंग स्ट्रैंड का एक अनुक्रम है। प्रतिलेखित mRNA का तदनुरुपी अनुक्रम क्या होगा?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand transcription coding conventions.
The sequence of transcribed mRNA is identical to the coding strand (sense strand) of DNA, except that thymine (\(\text{T}\)) in DNA is replaced by uracil (\(\text{U}\)) in RNA.

Step 2: Replace thymine with uracil.
Given coding strand sequence: \(\text{A-G-G-T-A-T-C-G-C-A-T}\)
Replacing \(\text{T}\) with \(\text{U}\) gives mRNA sequence: \(\text{A-G-G-U-A-U-C-G-C-A-U}\).

चरण 1: अनुलेखन कोडिंग परिपाटियों को समझें।
प्रतिलेखित mRNA का अनुक्रम डीएनए के कोडिंग स्ट्रैंड के समान होता है, सिवाय इसके कि डीएनए में थायमीन (\(\text{T}\)) को आरएनए में यूरेसिल (\(\text{U}\)) द्वारा प्रतिस्थापित किया जाता है।

चरण 2: थायमीन को यूरेसिल से प्रतिस्थापित करें।
दिया गया कोडिंग स्ट्रैंड अनुक्रम: \(\text{A-G-G-T-A-T-C-G-C-A-T}\)
\(\text{T}\) को \(\text{U}\) से बदलने पर mRNA अनुक्रम प्राप्त होता है: \(\text{A-G-G-U-A-U-C-G-C-A-U}\)।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MATCHING_MCQ_Q162 - Match menstrual cycle phases in Column I with Column II

questiontext.text:
Match the items given in Column I with those in Column II and select the correct option given below :

Column I Column II
a. Proliferative Phase i. Breakdown of endometrial lining
b. Secretory Phase ii. Follicular Phase
c. Menstruation iii. Luteal Phase

कॉलम I में दी गई वस्तुओं का कॉलम II से मिलान कीजिए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए :

कॉलम I कॉलम II
a. प्रचुरोद्भवन प्रावस्था (Proliferative Phase) i. गर्भाशय अंतःस्तर का विघटन
b. स्रावी प्रावस्था (Secretory Phase) ii. पुटकीय प्रावस्था (Follicular Phase)
c. आर्तव चक्र / रजोधर्म (Menstruation) iii. पीत प्रावस्था (Luteal Phase)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Match Proliferative Phase.
The proliferative phase of the uterus corresponds to the follicular phase of the ovary, during which primary follicles develop into mature Graafian follicles and endometrium regenerates.

Step 2: Match Secretory Phase.
The secretory phase corresponds to the luteal phase, during which the corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone to maintain endometrial lining.

Step 3: Match Menstruation.
Menstruation is characterized by the breakdown and shedding of the endometrial lining and blood vessels in the absence of fertilization.

Conclusion:
Matching each phase with its equivalent ovarian phase/process yields a-ii, b-iii, c-i.

चरण 1: प्रचुरोद्भवन प्रावस्था का मिलान करें।
गर्भाशय की प्रचुरोद्भवन प्रावस्था अंडाशय की पुटकीय प्रावस्था (follicular phase) के समतुल्य होती है, जिसके दौरान प्राथमिक पुटक परिपक्व ग्राफियन पुटक में विकसित होते हैं और अंतःस्तर पुनः उत्पन्न होता है।

चरण 2: स्रावी प्रावस्था का मिलान करें।
स्रावी प्रावस्था पीत प्रावस्था (luteal phase) के समतुल्य होती है, जिसके दौरान कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम गर्भाशय अंतःस्तर को बनाए रखने के लिए बड़ी मात्रा में प्रोजेस्टेरोन स्रावित करता है।

चरण 3: आर्तव/रजोधर्म का मिलान करें।
आर्तव स्राव निषेचन न होने की स्थिति में गर्भाशय अंतःस्तर और रक्त वाहिकाओं के टूटने और बहने से निरूपित होता है।

निष्कर्ष:
प्रत्येक प्रावस्था का उसके समतुल्य अंडाशयी प्रावस्था/प्रक्रिया से मिलान करने पर a-ii, b-iii, c-i प्राप्त होता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MATCHING_MCQ_Q163 - Match excretory disorders in Column I with Column II

questiontext.text:
Match the items given in Column I with those in Column II and select the correct option given below :

Column I Column II
a. Glycosuria i. Accumulation of uric acid in joints
b. Gout ii. Mass of crystallised salts within the kidney
c. Renal calculi iii. Inflammation in glomeruli
d. Glomerular nephritis iv. Presence of glucose in urine

कॉलम I में दी गई वस्तुओं का कॉलम II से मिलान कीजिए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए :

कॉलम I कॉलम II
a. ग्लाइकोसूरिया (Glycosuria) i. जोड़ों में यूरिक अम्ल का जमाव
b. गॉट (Gout) ii. वृक्क के भीतर क्रिस्टलीकृत लवणों का द्रव्यमान
c. रीनल कैल्कुलाई (Renal calculi) iii. ग्लोमेरुलस में शोथ (सूजन)
d. ग्लोमेरुलोनेफ्रैटिस (Glomerular nephritis) iv. मूत्र में ग्लूकोज की उपस्थिति

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Match Glycosuria.
Glycosuria is defined as the presence of glucose in urine, commonly indicative of diabetes mellitus.

Step 2: Match Gout.
Gout is a type of arthritis caused by the accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints, causing severe inflammation.

Step 3: Match Renal Calculi.
Renal calculi (kidney stones) are insoluble masses of crystallized salts (like oxalates) formed within the kidney.

Step 4: Match Glomerular Nephritis.
Glomerular nephritis is an inflammatory condition affecting the glomeruli of the kidneys.

Conclusion:
Matching each condition with its pathological description yields a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

चरण 1: ग्लाइकोसूरिया का मिलान करें।
ग्लाइकोसूरिया को मूत्र में ग्लूकोज की उपस्थिति के रूप में परिभाषित किया जाता है, जो सामान्यतः मधुमेह (diabetes mellitus) का सूचक है।

चरण 2: गॉट (Gout) का मिलान करें।
गॉट जोड़ों में यूरिक अम्ल क्रिस्टलों के संचयन के कारण होने वाला एक प्रकार का आर्थराइटिस (गठिया) है।

चरण 3: रीनल कैल्कुलाई का मिलान करें।
रीनल कैल्कुलाई (गुर्दे की पथरी) वृक्क के भीतर बने क्रिस्टलीकृत लवणों (जैसे ऑक्सालेट) के अघुलनशील द्रव्यमान हैं।

चरण 4: ग्लोमेरुलोनेफ्रैटिस का मिलान करें।
ग्लोमेरुलोनेफ्रैटिस वृक्क के केशिकागुच्छ (ग्लोमेरुलस) की एक शोथकारी (सूजन वाली) स्थिति है।

निष्कर्ष:
प्रत्येक विकार का उसके रोगविषयक विवरण से मिलान करने पर a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii प्राप्त होता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MATCHING_MCQ_Q164 - Match excretory system functions in Column I with Column II

questiontext.text:
Match the items given in Column I with those in Column II and select the correct option given below :

Column I (Function) Column II (Part of Excretory System)
a. Ultrafiltration i. Henle's loop
b. Concentration of urine ii. Ureter
c. Transport of urine iii. Urinary bladder
d. Storage of urine iv. Malpighian corpuscle
v. Proximal convoluted tubule

कॉलम I में दी गई वस्तुओं का कॉलम II से मिलान कीजिए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए :

कॉलम I (कार्य) कॉलम II (उत्सर्जी तंत्र का भाग)
a. परानिष्यंदन (Ultrafiltration) i. हेनले का लूप
b. मूत्र का सांद्रण (Concentration of urine) ii. मूत्रवाहिनी (Ureter)
c. मूत्र का परिवहन (Transport of urine) iii. मूत्राशय (Urinary bladder)
d. मूत्र का भंडारण (Storage of urine) iv. मालपिगी काय (Malpighian corpuscle)
v. समीपस्थ संवलित नलिका (Proximal convoluted tubule)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Match Ultrafiltration.
Ultrafiltration occurs across the glomerulus and Bowman's capsule, together forming the Malpighian corpuscle.

Step 2: Match Concentration of Urine.
Concentration of urine is carried out by the counter-current mechanism operated mainly by Henle's loop and vasa recta.

Step 3: Match Transport of Urine.
Transport of urine from the renal pelvis to the urinary bladder is conducted by the ureter.

Step 4: Match Storage of Urine.
Storage of urine temporarily before micturition occurs in the urinary bladder.

Conclusion:
Matching each function with the appropriate excretory structure yields a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

चरण 1: परानिष्यंदन का मिलान करें।
परानिष्यंदन (Ultrafiltration) ग्लोमेरुलस और बोमन कैप्सूल द्वारा होता है, जो मिलकर मालपिगी काय (Malpighian corpuscle) बनाते हैं।

चरण 2: मूत्र के सांद्रण का मिलान करें।
मूत्र का सांद्रण मुख्य रूप से हेनले के लूप और वासा रेक्टा द्वारा संचालित प्रतिधारा क्रियाविधि (counter-current mechanism) द्वारा किया जाता है।

चरण 3: मूत्र के परिवहन का मिलान करें।
वृक्क श्रोणि से मूत्राशय तक मूत्र का परिवहन मूत्रवाहिनी (ureter) द्वारा किया जाता है।

चरण 4: मूत्र के भंडारण का मिलान करें।
मूत्रत्याग से पूर्व मूत्र का अस्थायी भंडारण मूत्राशय (urinary bladder) में होता है।

निष्कर्ष:
प्रत्येक कार्य का उपयुक्त उत्सर्जी संरचना से मिलान करने पर a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii प्राप्त होता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q165 - Parietal cells indirectly help in erythropoiesis

questiontext.text:
Which of the following gastric cells indirectly help in erythropoiesis ?

निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी जठर कोशिकाएं अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से रक्ताणुउत्पत्ति (erythropoiesis) में सहायता करती हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Parietal cells (oxyntic cells) of the gastric mucosa secrete Castle's intrinsic factor alongside hydrochloric acid (\(\text{HCl}\)). Intrinsic factor is essential for the intestinal absorption of vitamin \(\text{B}_{12}\) (cyanocobalamin) in the terminal ileum. Vitamin \(\text{B}_{12}\) is crucial for the maturation of red blood cells during erythropoiesis. Thus, parietal cells indirectly aid in erythropoiesis.

जठर श्लेष्मिका की भित्तीय कोशिकाएं (Parietal cells / oxyntic cells) हाइड्रोक्लोरिक अम्ल (\(\text{HCl}\)) के साथ कैसल का आंतरिक कारक (Castle's intrinsic factor) स्रावित करती हैं। यह आंतरिक कारक अंत्य इलियम में विटामिन \(\text{B}_{12}\) के अवशोषण के लिए आवश्यक है। विटामिन \(\text{B}_{12}\) रक्ताणुउत्पत्ति (erythropoiesis) के दौरान लाल रक्त कोशिकाओं के परिपक्वता के लिए अत्यंत आवश्यक है। इस प्रकार, भित्तीय कोशिकाएं अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से रक्ताणुउत्पत्ति में सहायता करती हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MATCHING_MCQ_Q166 - Match plasma proteins in Column I with Column II

questiontext.text:
Match the items given in Column I with those in Column II and select the correct option given below :

Column I Column II
a. Fibrinogen i. Osmotic balance
b. Globulin ii. Blood clotting
c. Albumin iii. Defence mechanism

कॉलम I में दी गई वस्तुओं का कॉलम II से मिलान कीजिए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही विकल्प चुनिए :

कॉलम I कॉलम II
a. फाइब्रिनोजेन (Fibrinogen) i. परासरणी संतुलन (Osmotic balance)
b. ग्लोबुलिन (Globulin) ii. रक्त थक्का जमना (Blood clotting)
c. एल्ब्यूमिन (Albumin) iii. प्रतिरक्षा क्रियाविधि (Defence mechanism)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Match Fibrinogen.
Fibrinogen is an essential plasma protein required for blood coagulation/clotting.

Step 2: Match Globulin.
Globulins (specifically immunoglobulins) play a primary role in immune defense mechanisms of the body.

Step 3: Match Albumin.
Albumin helps maintain colloid osmotic pressure (osmotic balance) of blood plasma.

Conclusion:
Matching each protein with its physiological function gives a-ii, b-iii, c-i.

चरण 1: फाइब्रिनोजेन का मिलान करें।
फाइब्रिनोजेन रक्त के थक्के जमने (रक्त स्कंदन) के लिए आवश्यक एक प्रमुख प्लाज्मा प्रोटीन है।

चरण 2: ग्लोबुलिन का मिलान करें।
ग्लोबुलिन (विशेष रूप से इम्युनोग्लोबुलिन) शरीर की प्रतिरक्षा रक्षा क्रियाविधि में प्राथमिक भूमिका निभाते हैं।

चरण 3: एल्ब्यूमिन का मिलान करें।
एल्ब्यूमिन रक्त प्लाज्मा के परासरणी संतुलन (osmotic balance) को बनाए रखने में मदद करता है।

निष्कर्ष:
प्रत्येक प्लाज्मा प्रोटीन का उसके शारीरिक कार्य से मिलान करने पर a-ii, b-iii, c-i प्राप्त होता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q167 - Silicosis is an occupational respiratory disorder

questiontext.text:
Which of the following is an occupational respiratory disorder ?

निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा एक व्यवसायिक श्वसन विकार (occupational respiratory disorder) है?

generalfeedback.text:
Silicosis is an occupational respiratory disease caused by long-term inhalation of fine silica dust in stone-breaking, mining, and grinding industries. The chronic inhalation leads to severe inflammation, pulmonary fibrosis, and respiratory impairment. Botulism is a food poisoning caused by bacterial toxins, anthracis is a bacterial infection, and emphysema is a chronic respiratory condition mostly linked to cigarette smoking.

सिलिकोसिस (Silicosis) एक व्यवसायिक श्वसन विकार है जो पत्थर तोड़ने, खनन और घिसाई उद्योगों में सिलिका धूल के लंबे समय तक सांस द्वारा अंदर जाने से होता है। इसके लगातार संपर्क से फेफड़ों में गंभीर सूजन और रेशामयता (fibrosis) हो जाती है। बोटुलिज्म एक जीवाणु विषैलापन है, एंथ्रेकिस एक जीवाणु संक्रमण है, और वातस्फीति धूम्रपान से जुड़ा एक विकार है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q168 - Calcium binds to troponin removing masking on actin

questiontext.text:
Calcium is important in skeletal muscle contraction because it

कंकाल पेशी संकुचन में कैल्शियम महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह

generalfeedback.text:
During skeletal muscle excitation, calcium ions (\(\text{Ca}^{2+}\)) released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum bind to troponin C on the thin actin filaments. This binding induces a conformational change in the troponin-tropomyosin complex, displacing tropomyosin and unmasking the myosin-binding active sites on actin filaments, allowing cross-bridge formation and muscle contraction.

कंकाल पेशी उत्तेजन के दौरान, सार्कोप्लाज्मिक जालिका से विमुक्त कैल्शियम आयन (\(\text{Ca}^{2+}\)) पतले एक्टिन तंतुओं पर स्थित ट्रोपोनिन C से जुड़ते हैं। यह बंधन ट्रोपोनिन-ट्रोपियोमायोसिन सम्मिश्र में एक रूपरेखा परिवर्तन प्रेरित करता है, जिससे ट्रोपियोमायोसिन विस्थापित होकर एक्टिन पर मायोसिन-बंधन सक्रिय स्थलों से आवरण हटा देता है, जिससे क्रॉस-ब्रिज निर्माण और पेशी संकुचन संभव होता है।

answer.text: detaches the myosin head from the actin filament.
activates the myosin ATPase by binding to it.
binds to troponin to remove the masking of active sites on actin for myosin.
prevents the formation of bonds between the myosin cross bridges and the actin filament.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q169 - Nissl bodies composed of free ribosomes and RER

questiontext.text:
Nissl bodies are mainly composed of

निसल के काय (Nissl bodies) मुख्यतः किसके बने होते हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Nissl bodies (Nissl granules) located in the cyton (cell body) and dendrites of neurons are granular masses composed of free ribosomes and Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER). They are actively involved in protein synthesis required for neuronal function.

तंत्रिकाकोशिकाओं (neurons) के कोशिकाकाय (cyton) और द्रुमाश्म (dendrites) में स्थित निसल के काय (Nissl bodies) मुक्‍त राइबोसोमों और खुरदुरी अंतःप्रद्रव्यी जालिका (RER) के बने कणीकीय पिंड हैं। वे तंत्रिकीय कार्य के लिए आवश्यक प्रोटीन संश्लेषण में सक्रिय रूप से शामिल होते हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q170 - Oxidative phosphorylation takes place in inner mitochondrial membrane

questiontext.text:
Which of these statements is incorrect ?

इनमें से कौन-सा कथन गलत है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate oxidative phosphorylation location.
Oxidative phosphorylation (electron transport chain and ATP synthesis) takes place on the inner mitochondrial membrane (cristae), not the outer mitochondrial membrane. Therefore, this statement is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluate other statements.
- Glycolysis requires \(\text{NAD}^+\) to accept hydrogen atoms during the oxidation of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate.
- Glycolysis occurs in the cell cytosol.
- Soluble enzymes of the TCA cycle (except succinate dehydrogenase) are located in the mitochondrial matrix.

चरण 1: ऑक्सीकारी फॉस्फोरिलीकरण के स्थान का मूल्यांकन करें।
ऑक्सीकारी फॉस्फोरिलीकरण (इलेक्ट्रॉन परिवहन श्रृंखला और ATP संश्लेषण) आंतरिक सूत्रकणिका झिल्ली (क्रिस्टी) पर होता है, न कि बाहरी सूत्रकणिका झिल्ली पर। इसलिए यह कथन गलत है।

चरण 2: अन्य कथनों का मूल्यांकन करें।
- ग्लाइकोलाइसिस को ग्लिसराल्डिहाइड-3-फॉस्फेट के ऑक्सीकरण के दौरान हाइड्रोजन परमाणुओं को ग्रहण करने के लिए \(\text{NAD}^+\) की निरंतर आपूर्ति की आवश्यकता होती है।
- ग्लाइकोलाइसिस कोशिका के सायटोसॉल (कोशिकाद्रव्य) में होता है।
- TCA चक्र के घुलनशील एंजाइम सूत्रकणिका मैट्रिक्स (मादा) में उपस्थित होते हैं।

answer.text: Glycolysis operates as long as it is supplied with NAD that can pick up hydrogen atoms.
Enzymes of TCA cycle are present in mitochondrial matrix.
Oxidative phosphorylation takes place in outer mitochondrial membrane.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q171 - Polytene chromosomes in amphibian oocytes is incorrect match

questiontext.text:
Select the incorrect match :

गलत मिलान का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate polytene chromosomes pairing.
Polytene chromosomes (giant chromosomes) are found in salivary glands of dipteran insect larvae (e.g., Drosophila), whereas lampbrush chromosomes are found in the diplotene oocytes of amphibians. Hence, pairing polytene chromosomes with amphibian oocytes is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluate remaining matches.
- Submetacentric chromosomes appear L-shaped during anaphase movement.
- Allosomes are sex chromosomes that determine sex.
- Lampbrush chromosomes are observed in diplotene bivalents during meiotic prophase-I.

चरण 1: पॉलीटीन गुणसूत्र युग्मन का मूल्यांकन करें।
पॉलीटीन गुणसूत्र (विशाल गुणसूत्र) डिप्टेरन कीट लार्वा (जैसे Drosophila) की लार ग्रंथियों में पाए जाते हैं, जबकि लैंपब्रश गुणसूत्र उभयचरों के द्विपट्ट ओसाइट्स में पाए जाते हैं। अतः पॉलीटीन गुणसूत्रों को उभयचरों के ओसाइट्स के साथ सुमेलित करना गलत है।

चरण 2: शेष जोड़ों का मूल्यांकन करें।
- सबमेटासेंट्रिक गुणसूत्र एनाफेज गति के दौरान L-आकार के दिखाई देते हैं।
- एलोसोम लिंग गुणसूत्र (sex chromosomes) हैं जो लिंग का निर्धारण करते हैं।
- अर्धसूत्री प्रोफेज-I के दौरान द्विपट्ट युग्मियों में लैंपब्रश गुणसूत्र देखे जाते हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q172 - Human dentition described as Thecodont Diphyodont Heterodont

questiontext.text:
Which of the following terms describe human dentition ?

निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से शब्द मानव दंत-विन्यास को निरूपित करते हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Human dentition is described by three features:
1. Thecodont: Teeth are embedded in individual sockets of jaw bones.
2. Diphyodont: Two sets of teeth develop during life — temporary/deciduous teeth replaced by permanent/adult teeth.
3. Heterodont: Teeth are of different structural types (incisors, canines, premolars, and molars).

मानव दंत-विन्यास को तीन विशेषताओं द्वारा वर्णित किया जाता है:
1. गर्तदंती (Thecodont): दाँत जबड़े की हड्डियों के खाँचों (sockets) में धँसे होते हैं।
2. द्विबारदंती (Diphyodont): जीवनकाल में दो बार दाँत निकलते हैं — अस्थाई/दूध के दाँत जो स्थाई दाँतों द्वारा प्रतिस्थापित होते हैं।
3. विषमदंती (Heterodont): दाँत विभिन्न प्रकार की आकृतियों के होते हैं (कृंतक, रदनक, अग्रचर्वणक और चर्वणक)।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q173 - Phospholipid synthesis does not occur in RER

questiontext.text:
Which of the following events does not occur in rough endoplasmic reticulum ?

निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी घटना खुरदुरी अंतःप्रद्रव्यी जालिका (RER) में नहीं होती है?

generalfeedback.text:
Phospholipid and lipid synthesis occurs primarily in the Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER). The Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER) is specialized for protein synthesis, signal peptide cleavage, protein folding (assisted by chaperones), and initial N-linked protein glycosylation.

फॉस्फोलिपिड और लिपिड का संश्लेषण मुख्य रूप से चिकनी अंतःप्रद्रव्यी जालिका (SER) में होता है। खुरदुरी अंतःप्रद्रव्यी जालिका (RER) प्रोटीन संश्लेषण, सिग्नल पेप्टाइड के विखंडन, प्रोटीन वलन (folding), और प्रारंभिक प्रोटीन ग्लाइकोसिलेशन के लिए विशिष्ट होती है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q174 - Multiple ribosomes associated with mRNA form polysome

questiontext.text:
Many ribosomes may associate with a single mRNA to form multiple copies of a polypeptide simultaneously. Such strings of ribosomes are termed as

एक ही mRNA से अनेक राइबोसोम जुड़कर एक साथ एक पॉलीपेप्टाइड की कई प्रतियां बना सकते हैं। राइबोसोम की ऐसी शृंखलाओं को क्या कहा जाता है?

generalfeedback.text:
A aggregate string of multiple ribosomes bound to a single mRNA molecule translating protein polypeptide chains concurrently is called a polyribosome or polysome.

एक ही mRNA अणु से बंधे अनेक राइबोसोम की एक शृंखला जो एक साथ प्रोटीन पॉलीपेप्टाइड शृंखलाओं का अनुवादन करती है, बहुराइबोसोम (polyribosome) या पॉलीसोम (polysome) कहलाती है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q175 - Elephantiasis causes chronic inflammation of lymphatic vessels

questiontext.text:
In which disease does mosquito transmitted pathogen cause chronic inflammation of lymphatic vessels ?

किस रोग में मच्छर द्वारा संचारित रोगजनक लसीका वाहिकाओं का दीर्घकालिक शोथ (सूजन) उत्पन्न करता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Elephantiasis (filariasis) is caused by filarial worms (Wuchereria bancrofti and Wuchereria malayi), which are transmitted through the bite of infected female Culex mosquitoes. The adult worms live in lymphatic vessels, causing chronic inflammation and severe swelling (lymphedema) of lower limbs and genital organs.

हाथीपांव / फीलपांव (Elephantiasis / filariasis) फाइलेरिया कृमियों (Wuchereria bancrofti और Wuchereria malayi) के कारण होता है, जो संक्रमित मादा Culex मच्छरों के काटने से फैलते हैं। वयस्क कृमि लसीका वाहिकाओं में रहते हैं, जिससे लसीका वाहिकाओं में दीर्घकालिक सूजन और निचले अंगों तथा जननांगों में अत्यधिक सूजन हो जाती है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q176 - Alzheimers disease is not an autoimmune disease

questiontext.text:
Which of the following is not an autoimmune disease ?

निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा स्वप्रतिरक्षा रोग (autoimmune disease) नहीं है?

generalfeedback.text:
Alzheimer's disease is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive memory loss and cognitive decline due to extracellular amyloid-beta plaques and neurofibrillary tangles. Rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis, and vitiligo are autoimmune disorders where the body's immune system attacks its own cells and tissues.

अल्जाइमर रोग (Alzheimer's disease) एक तंत्रिका-अपह्रासी (neurodegenerative) विकार है जो बाह्यकोशकीय एमाइलॉइड-बीटा पट्टिकाओं और न्यूरोफाइब्रिलरी टेंगल्स के कारण प्रगतिशील स्मृति हानि का कारण बनता है। आमवाती संधिशोथ (Rheumatoid arthritis), सोरायसिस, और विटिलिगो स्वप्रतिरक्षा विकार हैं जहाँ प्रतिरक्षा तंत्र शरीर की अपनी कोशिकाओं पर हमला करता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q177 - Eye of octopus bat and man represents convergent evolution

questiontext.text:
Among the following sets of examples for divergent evolution, select the incorrect option :

अपसारी विकास (divergent evolution) के उदाहरणों के निम्नलिखित सेटों में से गलत विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
The eyes of Octopus and mammals (bat, human) are analogous structures representing convergent evolution (analogous organs having different embryonic origins but performing similar visual functions). Vertebrate forelimbs, hearts, and brains share common embryonic ancestry and structural plan, exemplifying homologous organs and divergent evolution.

ऑक्टोपस और स्तनधारियों (चमगादड़, मनुष्य) की आँखें अभिसारी विकास (convergent evolution) को निरूपित करने वाली समवृत्ति संरचनाएं हैं (भिन्न भ्रूणीय उत्पत्ति लेकिन समान दृष्टि कार्य)। कशेरुकियों के अग्रपाद, हृदय और मस्तिष्क सामान्य भ्रूणीय पूर्वज और संरचनात्मक योजना साझा करते हैं, जो समजात अंगों और अपसारी विकास (divergent evolution) के उदाहरण हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q178 - Curd formation increases Vitamin B12

questiontext.text:
Conversion of milk to curd improves its nutritional value by increasing the amount of

दूध का दही में रूपांतरण किसकी मात्रा बढ़ाकर इसके पोषण मूल्य में सुधार करता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Lactic Acid Bacteria (LAB) like Lactobacillus convert milk to curd. During fermentation, LAB synthesize significant amounts of Vitamin \(\text{B}_{12}\), thereby enhancing the nutritional quality of curd over milk.

Lactobacillus जैसे लैक्टिक एसिड बैक्टीरिया (LAB) दूध को दही में बदलते हैं। किण्वन के दौरान, LAB विटामिन \(\text{B}_{12}\) की महत्वपूर्ण मात्रा का संश्लेषण करते हैं, जिससे दूध की तुलना में दही की पोषण गुणवत्ता बढ़ जाती है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q179 - Similarity of bone structure in vertebrate forelimbs is homology

questiontext.text:
The similarity of bone structure in the forelimbs of many vertebrates is an example of

अनेक कशेरुकियों के अग्रपादों की अस्थि संरचना में समानता किसका उदाहरण है?

generalfeedback.text:
Homology refers to organs having a common anatomical origin and basic structural framework (e.g. humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals) adapted to different functions in different species due to divergent evolution. Examples include forelimbs of whales, bats, cheetahs, and humans.

समजातता (Homology) उन अंगों को संदर्भित करती है जिनकी शारीरिक उत्पत्ति और मूलभूत संरचनात्मक ढांचा समान होता है, लेकिन अपसारी विकास के कारण विभिन्न प्रजातियों में विभिन्न कार्यों के लिए अनुकूलित होते हैं। उदाहरणों में व्हेल, चमगादड़, चीता और मनुष्य के अग्रपाद शामिल हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2018_MCQ_Q180 - Human blood groups inheritance involves Dominance Co-dominance Multiple allele

questiontext.text:
Which of the following characteristics represent 'Inheritance of blood groups' in humans ?
a. Dominance
b. Co-dominance
c. Multiple allele
d. Incomplete dominance
e. Polygenic inheritance

निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी विशेषताएं मनुष्यों में 'रक्त समूहों की वंशानुगति' को दर्शाती हैं?
a. प्रभाविता (Dominance)
b. सह-प्रभाविता (Co-dominance)
c. बहु एलील (Multiple allele)
d. अपूर्ण प्रभाविता (Incomplete dominance)
e. बहुजीनी वंशानुगति (Polygenic inheritance)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze ABO blood group genetics.
The ABO blood group system is controlled by the gene \(I\), which has three alleles: \(I^A\), \(I^B\), and \(i\).

Step 2: Evaluate genetic phenomena.
- Dominance: Alleles \(I^A\) and \(I^B\) are completely dominant over allele \(i\).
- Co-dominance: When both \(I^A\) and \(I^B\) are present together in genotype \(I^A I^B\), both express fully, resulting in AB blood group.
- Multiple allele: The gene \(I\) exists in three alternative allelic forms (\(I^A\), \(I^B\), \(i\)) in the human population.

Conclusion:
Human blood group inheritance exhibits Dominance (a), Co-dominance (b), and Multiple allele (c).

चरण 1: ABO रक्त समूह आनुवंशिकी का विश्लेषण करें।
ABO रक्त समूह प्रणाली जीन \(I\) द्वारा नियंत्रित होती है, जिसके तीन एलील हैं: \(I^A\), \(I^B\), और \(i\)।

चरण 2: आनुवंशिक परिघटनाओं का मूल्यांकन करें।
- प्रभाविता (Dominance): एलील \(I^A\) और \(I^B\) एलील \(i\) पर पूर्णतः प्रभावी हैं।
- सह-प्रभाविता (Co-dominance): जब \(I^A\) और \(I^B\) दोनों जीनोटाइप \(I^A I^B\) में एक साथ उपस्थित होते हैं, तो दोनों पूर्णतः अभिव्यक्त होते हैं, जिससे AB रक्त समूह बनता है।
- बहु एलील (Multiple allele): मानव समष्टि में जीन \(I\) तीन वैकल्पिक एलीली रूपों (\(I^A\), \(I^B\), \(i\)) में मौजूद है।

निष्कर्ष:
मानव रक्त समूह की वंशानुगति प्रभाविता (a), सह-प्रभाविता (b), और बहु एलील (c) को प्रदर्शित करती है।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q01 - Electric field inside and outside hollow metal sphere

questiontext.text: A hollow metal sphere of radius \( R \) is uniformly charged. The electric field due to the sphere at a distance \( r \) from the centre

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
Inside a uniformly charged hollow metal sphere of radius \( R \), the electrostatic potential is constant throughout the interior volume and equal to its value at the surface. Consequently, the electric field intensity inside the shell (\( r < R \)) is zero everywhere.

Evaluation
Outside the sphere (\( r > R \)), the entire charge behaves as if concentrated at the center. The electric field is given by Coulomb's law: \( E = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{Q}{r^2} \). Thus, as distance \( r \) increases for \( r > R \), the magnitude of the field decreases inversely proportional to \( r^2 \).

Final Conclusion
The electric field due to the sphere is zero as \( r \) increases for \( r < R \), and decreases as \( r \) increases for \( r > R \).

answer.text: zero as \( r \) increases for \( r < R \), decreases as \( r \) increases for \( r > R \)
zero as \( r \) increases for \( r < R \), increases as \( r \) increases for \( r > R \)
decreases as \( r \) increases for \( r < R \) and for \( r > R \)
increases as \( r \) increases for \( r < R \) and for \( r > R \)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q02 - Work done by a variable force along y direction

questiontext.text: A force \( F = 20 + 10y \) acts on a particle in \( y \)-direction where \( F \) is in newton and \( y \) in meter. Work done by this force to move the particle from \( y = 0 \) to \( y = 1\text{ m} \) is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Force expression: \( F = 20 + 10y \text{ N} \)
Initial position: \( y_i = 0\text{ m} \)
Final position: \( y_f = 1\text{ m} \)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The force acts along the positive \( y \)-direction, and the displacement occurs along the positive \( y \)-axis.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Work done by a position-dependent variable force is defined by: \[ W = \int_{y_i}^{y_f} F \, dy \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the force function into the integral: \[ W = \int_0^1 (20 + 10y) \, dy \] \[ W = \left[ 20y + 5y^2 \right]_0^1 \] \[ W = (20(1) + 5(1)^2) - (0) = 20 + 5 = 25\text{ J} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The total work done by the force to displace the particle from \( y = 0 \) to \( y = 1\text{ m} \) is \( 25\text{ J} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q03 - Power consumption ratio of glowing bulbs

questiontext.text: Six similar bulbs are connected as shown in the figure with a DC source of emf \( E \), and zero internal resistance. The ratio of power consumption by the bulbs when (i) all are glowing and (ii) in the situation when two from section A and one from section B are glowing, will be

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Let the resistance of each identical bulb be \( R \).
DC source voltage = \( E \), internal resistance = \( 0 \).
Section A has 3 bulbs connected in parallel, and Section B has 3 bulbs connected in parallel. Sections A and B are in series connection across the source.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Power consumed by the combination connected across constant emf \( E \) is given by \( P = \frac{E^2}{R_{\text{eq}}} \).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Equivalent resistance of \( n \) identical resistors in parallel: \( R_p = \frac{R}{n} \).
Total equivalent resistance of series sections: \( R_{\text{eq}} = R_A + R_B \).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Case (i): All 6 bulbs glowing.
Resistance of section A: \( R_A = \frac{R}{3} \).
Resistance of section B: \( R_B = \frac{R}{3} \).
Total equivalent resistance: \[ R_{\text{eq1}} = \frac{R}{3} + \frac{R}{3} = \frac{2R}{3} \]
Power consumption in Case (i): \[ P_1 = \frac{E^2}{R_{\text{eq1}}} = \frac{E^2}{\frac{2R}{3}} = \frac{3E^2}{2R} \]

Case (ii): Two bulbs from section A and one bulb from section B glowing.
Resistance of section A: \( R_A' = \frac{R}{2} \).
Resistance of section B: \( R_B' = R \).
Total equivalent resistance: \[ R_{\text{eq2}} = \frac{R}{2} + R = \frac{3R}{2} \]
Power consumption in Case (ii): \[ P_2 = \frac{E^2}{R_{\text{eq2}}} = \frac{E^2}{\frac{3R}{2}} = \frac{2E^2}{3R} \]

Ratio of power consumption \( P_1 : P_2 \): \[ \frac{P_1}{P_2} = \frac{\frac{3E^2}{2R}}{\frac{2E^2}{3R}} = \frac{3}{2} \times \frac{3}{2} = \frac{9}{4} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio of power consumption between the two situations is \( 9:4 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q04 - Depth of water corresponding to excess pressure in soap bubble

questiontext.text: A soap bubble, having radius of \( 1\text{ mm} \), is blown from a detergent solution having a surface tension of \( 2.5 \times 10^{-2}\text{ N/m} \). The pressure inside the bubble equals at a point \( Z_0 \) below the free surface of water in a container. Taking \( g = 10\text{ m/s}^2 \), density of water \( = 10^3\text{ kg/m}^3 \), the value of \( Z_0 \) is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Radius of soap bubble \( r = 1\text{ mm} = 10^{-3}\text{ m} \)
Surface tension \( T = 2.5 \times 10^{-2}\text{ N/m} \)
Acceleration due to gravity \( g = 10\text{ m/s}^2 \)
Density of water \( \rho = 10^3\text{ kg/m}^3 \)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Atmospheric pressure is \( P_0 \). A soap bubble has two spherical interfaces (inner and outer liquid surfaces).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Excess pressure inside a soap bubble: \[ \Delta P = \frac{4T}{r} \]
Total pressure inside the bubble: \[ P_{\text{in}} = P_0 + \frac{4T}{r} \]
Hydrostatic pressure at depth \( Z_0 \) in water: \[ P_{\text{water}} = P_0 + \rho g Z_0 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Equate the pressure inside the bubble to the pressure at depth \( Z_0 \): \[ P_0 + \frac{4T}{r} = P_0 + \rho g Z_0 \implies \rho g Z_0 = \frac{4T}{r} \]
Substitute given numerical values: \[ \frac{4T}{r} = \frac{4 \times 2.5 \times 10^{-2}\text{ N/m}}{10^{-3}\text{ m}} = 100\text{ N/m}^2 \]
Equating hydrostatic pressure difference: \[ (10^3\text{ kg/m}^3) \times (10\text{ m/s}^2) \times Z_0 = 100\text{ N/m}^2 \] \[ 10^4 Z_0 = 100 \implies Z_0 = \frac{100}{10^4} = 10^{-2}\text{ m} = 1\text{ cm} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The depth \( Z_0 \) below the free surface of water is \( 1\text{ cm} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q05 - Wavelength order of visible light spectrum

questiontext.text: Which colour of the light has the longest wavelength?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
In the visible spectrum of electromagnetic radiation, wavelength increases continuously from violet to red light according to the relation \( c = \nu \lambda \).

Evaluation
The approximate range of wavelengths for visible spectrum colors is:
- Violet: \( 380 - 450\text{ nm} \)
- Blue: \( 450 - 495\text{ nm} \)
- Green: \( 495 - 570\text{ nm} \)
- Red: \( 620 - 750\text{ nm} \)
Red light possesses the lowest frequency and therefore the longest wavelength among all visible spectrum colors.

Final Conclusion
Red light has the longest wavelength.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q06 - Acceleration due to gravity and weight at depth

questiontext.text: A body weight 200 N on the surface of earth. How much will it weight half way down to the centre of the earth?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Weight of body on Earth's surface \( W = mg = 200\text{ N} \).
Depth below surface \( d = \frac{R}{2} \), where \( R \) is the radius of the Earth.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Earth is assumed to be a uniform sphere of uniform mass density.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Acceleration due to gravity at depth \( d \) inside the Earth is given by: \[ g' = g \left(1 - \frac{d}{R}\right) \]
The weight at depth \( d \) is: \[ W' = mg' \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute \( d = \frac{R}{2} \) into the gravity formula: \[ g' = g \left(1 - \frac{R/2}{R}\right) = g \left(1 - \frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{g}{2} \]
Calculate the weight at depth \( d \): \[ W' = m\left(\frac{g}{2}\right) = \frac{mg}{2} = \frac{200\text{ N}}{2} = 100\text{ N} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Halfway down to the center of the Earth, the acceleration due to gravity halves, so the weight of the body becomes \( 100\text{ N} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q07 - Rate of flow of water from orifice near bottom

questiontext.text: A small hole of area of cross-section 2 mm² present near the bottom of a fully filled open tank of height 2 m. Taking g = 10 m/s², the rate of flow of water through the open hole would be nearly

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Area of cross-section of hole \( A = 2\text{ mm}^2 = 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2 \)
Height of water column \( h = 2\text{ m} \)
Acceleration due to gravity \( g = 10\text{ m/s}^2 \)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Water is treated as an ideal incompressible, non-viscous fluid flowing under Torricelli's theorem conditions.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Speed of efflux from a small hole at depth \( h \): \[ v = \sqrt{2gh} \]
Volume flow rate (rate of flow): \[ Q = A \cdot v \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate speed of efflux: \[ v = \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 2} = \sqrt{40} \approx 6.3245\text{ m/s} \]
Calculate volume flow rate: \[ Q = (2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2) \times (6.3245\text{ m/s}) \approx 12.649 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3\text{/s} \approx 12.6 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3\text{/s} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The rate of flow of water through the hole is approximately \( 12.6 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3\text{/s} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q08 - Work required to stop a rolling disc

questiontext.text: A disc of radius 2 m and mass 100 kg rolls on a horizontal floor. Its centre of mass has speed of 20 cm/s. How much work is needed to stop it?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of disc \( m = 100\text{ kg} \)
Radius of disc \( R = 2\text{ m} \)
Speed of centre of mass \( v = 20\text{ cm/s} = 0.2\text{ m/s} \)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The disc undergoes pure rolling without slipping on a horizontal plane surface.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Total kinetic energy of a rolling body: \[ K_{\text{total}} = K_{\text{trans}} + K_{\text{rot}} = \frac{1}{2} m v^2 + \frac{1}{2} I \omega^2 \]
For a solid disc, moment of inertia \( I = \frac{1}{2} m R^2 \), and pure rolling condition yields \( \omega = \frac{v}{R} \).
By the Work-Energy theorem, work required to bring the body to rest equals its total initial kinetic energy: \( W = K_{\text{total}} \).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute \( I \) and \( \omega \) into kinetic energy: \[ K_{\text{total}} = \frac{1}{2} m v^2 + \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{1}{2} m R^2\right)\left(\frac{v}{R}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{2} m v^2 + \frac{1}{4} m v^2 = \frac{3}{4} m v^2 \]
Substitute numerical values: \[ W = \frac{3}{4} \times 100 \times (0.2)^2 = 75 \times 0.04 = 3\text{ J} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The work required to stop the rolling disc is \( 3\text{ J} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q09 - Equivalent focal length of thin lens combination with liquid

questiontext.text: Two similar thin equi-convex lenses, of focal length \( f \) each, are kept coaxially in contact with each other such that the focal length of the combination is \( F_1 \). When the space between the two lenses is filled with glycerin (which has the same refractive index (\( \mu = 1.5 \)) as that of glass) then the equivalent focal length is \( F_2 \). The ratio \( F_1 : F_2 \) will be

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Focal length of each equi-convex glass lens = \( f \)
Refractive index of glass \( \mu_g = 1.5 \)
Refractive index of glycerin \( \mu_l = 1.5 \)
Combination 1: Two convex lenses in contact without glycerin, equivalent focal length = \( F_1 \).
Combination 2: Space between lenses filled with glycerin, equivalent focal length = \( F_2 \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Lenses are thin and kept coaxially in contact. Cartesian sign convention applies.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Lens Maker's Formula: \[ \frac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right) \]
Equivalent focal length of thin lenses in contact: \[ \frac{1}{F} = \sum \frac{1}{f_i} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
1. For Combination 1 (two convex glass lenses): \[ \frac{1}{F_1} = \frac{1}{f} + \frac{1}{f} = \frac{2}{f} \implies F_1 = \frac{f}{2} \]
2. Find radius of curvature \( R \) of equi-convex glass lens: \[ \frac{1}{f} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R} - \left(-\frac{1}{R}\right)\right) = 0.5 \times \frac{2}{R} = \frac{1}{R} \implies R = f \]
3. The glycerin filled in the gap forms an equi-concave liquid lens with radii of curvature \( -R \) and \( +R \). Its focal length \( f_l \) is: \[ \frac{1}{f_l} = (1.5 - 1)\left(-\frac{1}{R} - \frac{1}{R}\right) = 0.5 \times \left(-\frac{2}{R}\right) = -\frac{1}{R} = -\frac{1}{f} \implies f_l = -f \]
4. For Combination 2 (two convex glass lenses + one concave liquid lens in contact): \[ \frac{1}{F_2} = \frac{1}{f} + \frac{1}{f_l} + \frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{f} - \frac{1}{f} + \frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{f} \implies F_2 = f \]
5. Ratio \( F_1 : F_2 \): \[ \frac{F_1}{F_2} = \frac{f/2}{f} = \frac{1}{2} = 1:2 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio \( F_1 : F_2 \) is \( 1:2 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q10 - Maximum percentage error calculation in composite physical quantity

questiontext.text: In an experiment, the percentage of error occurred in the measurement of physical quantities A, B, C and D are 1%, 2%, 3% and 4% respectively. Then the maximum percentage of error in the measurement X, where \( X = \frac{A^2 B^{1/2}}{C^{1/3} D^3} \), will be

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Physical quantity relation: \[ X = \frac{A^2 B^{1/2}}{C^{1/3} D^3} \]
Percentage errors:
\( \frac{\Delta A}{A} \times 100 = 1\% \)
\( \frac{\Delta B}{B} \times 100 = 2\% \)
\( \frac{\Delta C}{C} \times 100 = 3\% \)
\( \frac{\Delta D}{D} \times 100 = 4\% \)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Maximum percentage error is calculated by adding the absolute maximum fractional errors of each independent variable weighted by their respective power exponents.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
For a expression \( X = A^a B^b C^{-c} D^{-d} \), maximum percentage error is: \[ \frac{\Delta X}{X} \times 100 = |a| \left(\frac{\Delta A}{A}\times 100\right) + |b| \left(\frac{\Delta B}{B}\times 100\right) + |c| \left(\frac{\Delta C}{C}\times 100\right) + |d| \left(\frac{\Delta D}{D}\times 100\right) \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute exponents and values into the equation: \[ \frac{\Delta X}{X} \times 100 = 2(1\%) + \frac{1}{2}(2\%) + \frac{1}{3}(3\%) + 3(4\%) \] \[ \frac{\Delta X}{X} \times 100 = 2\% + 1\% + 1\% + 12\% = 16\% \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The maximum percentage error in \( X \) is \( 16\% \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q11 - SI unit of thermal conductivity

questiontext.text: The unit of thermal conductivity is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Physical quantity: Thermal Conductivity (\( K \)).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Heat flows in steady state across a material of cross-sectional area \( A \) and thickness \( L \) under a temperature difference \( \Delta T \).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Heat transfer rate equation: \[ \frac{Q}{t} = K \frac{A \Delta T}{L} \implies K = \frac{Q}{t} \cdot \frac{L}{A \Delta T} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Identify SI units of constituent variables:
- Rate of heat flow \( \frac{Q}{t} \): Watt (\text{W})
- Thickness \( L \): meter (\text{m})
- Area \( A \): square meter (\text{m}^2)
- Temperature difference \( \Delta T \): Kelvin (\text{K})

Substitute SI units into the formula for \( K \): \[ [K] = \frac{\text{W} \cdot \text{m}}{\text{m}^2 \cdot \text{K}} = \text{W m}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The SI unit of thermal conductivity is \( \text{W m}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q12 - Work done to raise mass to height equal to radius of Earth

questiontext.text: The work done to raise a mass \( m \) from the surface of the earth to a height \( h \), which is equal to the radius of the earth, is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of body = \( m \)
Height above Earth's surface \( h = R \), where \( R \) is the radius of Earth.
Acceleration due to gravity at surface = \( g \)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Gravitational potential energy is zero at infinite separation. The gravitational field varies with distance for height comparable to Earth's radius.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Gravitational potential energy at distance \( r \) from Earth's center: \[ U(r) = -\frac{GMm}{r} \]
Work done by external force equals change in potential energy: \[ W = \Delta U = U_f - U_i \]
Relation between gravitational constant and surface gravity: \( GM = gR^2 \)

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Initial position (surface): \( r_i = R \implies U_i = -\frac{GMm}{R} \)
Final position (height \( h = R \)): \( r_f = R + R = 2R \implies U_f = -\frac{GMm}{2R} \)
Calculate work done: \[ W = -\frac{GMm}{2R} - \left(-\frac{GMm}{R}\right) = \frac{GMm}{2R} \]
Substitute \( GM = gR^2 \): \[ W = \frac{(gR^2) m}{2R} = \frac{1}{2} mgR \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The work done to raise the mass to height equal to the radius of Earth is \( \frac{1}{2} mgR \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q13 - Thermodynamic process with no heat exchange

questiontext.text: In which of the following processes, heat is neither absorbed nor released by a system?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
By definition in thermodynamics, an adiabatic process is one in which no heat energy crosses the boundary of the system (\( \Delta Q = 0 \)).

Evaluation
- Isobaric process: pressure remains constant; heat is exchanged with surroundings (\( Q = n C_p \Delta T \)).
- Isochoric process: volume remains constant; heat is exchanged with surroundings (\( Q = n C_v \Delta T \)).
- Isothermal process: temperature remains constant; heat exchange equals work done (\( Q = W \)).
- Adiabatic process: system is thermally insulated from surroundings, so heat is neither absorbed nor released.

Final Conclusion
An adiabatic process is the thermodynamic process where heat is neither absorbed nor released.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q14 - Force between point charges after charge transfer

questiontext.text: Two point charges A and B, having charges \( +Q \) and \( -Q \) respectively, are placed at certain distance apart and force acting between them is F. If \( 25\% \) charge of A is transferred to B, then force between the charges becomes

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial charge of A: \( Q_A = +Q \)
Initial charge of B: \( Q_B = -Q \)
Initial distance: \( r \)
Initial electrostatic force magnitude: \( F \)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Coulomb's Law applies to stationary point charges in free space.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Coulomb's Law: \[ F = k \frac{|Q_A Q_B|}{r^2} = k \frac{Q^2}{r^2} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Amount of charge transferred from A to B: \( \Delta Q = 0.25 Q = \frac{Q}{4} \)
New charge on A: \[ Q_A' = Q - \frac{Q}{4} = \frac{3}{4} Q \]
New charge on B: \[ Q_B' = -Q + \frac{Q}{4} = -\frac{3}{4} Q \]
Calculate new electrostatic force magnitude \( F' \): \[ F' = k \frac{|Q_A' Q_B'|}{r^2} = k \frac{\left(\frac{3}{4} Q\right)\left(\frac{3}{4} Q\right)}{r^2} = \frac{9}{16} \left(k \frac{Q^2}{r^2}\right) = \frac{9F}{16} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The force between the charges becomes \( \frac{9F}{16} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q15 - Boolean logic operation of LED circuit

questiontext.text: The correct Boolean operation represented by the circuit diagram drawn is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
A DC voltage source of \( +6\text{ V} \) is connected to two resistors \( R \) and an LED (\( Y \)).
Two switches \( A \) and \( B \) can take state 0 (open) or state 1 (connected to common line).

Step 2: Circuit Analysis and Truth Table Construction
- When \( A = 0 \) and \( B = 0 \): Both switches are open. Current flows from \( +6\text{ V} \) through the upper resistor, LED, and lower resistor to ground. The LED glows, giving output \( Y = 1 \).
- When \( A = 1 \) and \( B = 0 \): Upper node is connected to the common line, but lower node remains ungrounded via switch B. Current continues to flow through the LED, so \( Y = 1 \).
- When \( A = 0 \) and \( B = 1 \): Lower node is connected to the common line, but upper node is not connected to common line via switch A. Current continues to flow through the LED, so \( Y = 1 \).
- When \( A = 1 \) and \( B = 1 \): Both switches connect both terminals of the LED directly to the same common line, effectively short-circuiting the LED. Potential difference across the LED becomes zero, so no current passes through it and the LED turns off, giving output \( Y = 0 \).

Step 3: Boolean Evaluation
The output is 0 only when both inputs are 1, and 1 for all other input combinations. This matches the truth table of a NAND operation: \[ Y = \overline{A \cdot B} \]

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The logic circuit represents a NAND gate.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q16 - Identification of circuit protection device

questiontext.text: Which of the following acts as a circuit protection device?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
A circuit protection device protects electrical circuits and components by automatically breaking the current flow whenever an overcurrent or short-circuit condition occurs.

Evaluation
- Inductor: stores energy in a magnetic field and opposes changes in current, but does not disconnect the circuit.
- Switch: manually opens or closes a circuit under normal operation.
- Fuse: contains a metallic strip with a low melting point that melts and breaks the circuit when current exceeds a safe value.
- Conductor: carries electric current without intention of breaking.

Final Conclusion
A fuse acts as a circuit protection device.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q17 - Thermal expansion and temperature independent length difference

questiontext.text: A copper rod of \( 88\text{ cm} \) and an aluminium rod of unknown length have their increase in length independent of increase in temperature. The length of aluminium rod is (\( \alpha_{\text{Cu}} = 1.7 \times 10^{-5}\text{ K}^{-1} \) and \( \alpha_{\text{Al}} = 2.2 \times 10^{-5}\text{ K}^{-1} \))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length of copper rod \( L_{\text{Cu}} = 88\text{ cm} \)
Coefficient of linear expansion of copper \( \alpha_{\text{Cu}} = 1.7 \times 10^{-5}\text{ K}^{-1} \)
Coefficient of linear expansion of aluminium \( \alpha_{\text{Al}} = 2.2 \times 10^{-5}\text{ K}^{-1} \)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The condition that the difference in lengths remains constant for any temperature change \( \Delta T \) requires the absolute expansion in both rods to be equal: \( \Delta L_{\text{Cu}} = \Delta L_{\text{Al}} \).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Linear expansion formula: \[ \Delta L = L \alpha \Delta T \]
Equating expansions: \[ L_{\text{Cu}} \alpha_{\text{Cu}} \Delta T = L_{\text{Al}} \alpha_{\text{Al}} \Delta T \implies L_{\text{Cu}} \alpha_{\text{Cu}} = L_{\text{Al}} \alpha_{\text{Al}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Rearrange for \( L_{\text{Al}} \): \[ L_{\text{Al}} = \frac{L_{\text{Cu}} \alpha_{\text{Cu}}}{\alpha_{\text{Al}}} \]
Substitute numerical values: \[ L_{\text{Al}} = \frac{88\text{ cm} \times (1.7 \times 10^{-5}\text{ K}^{-1})}{2.2 \times 10^{-5}\text{ K}^{-1}} = \frac{88}{2.2} \times 1.7 = 40 \times 1.7 = 68\text{ cm} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The length of the aluminium rod is \( 68\text{ cm} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q18 - Conduction and displacement current in charging capacitor

questiontext.text: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance \( 20\ \mu\text{F} \) is being charged by a voltage source whose potential is changing at the rate of \( 3\text{ V/s} \). The conduction current through the connecting wires, and the displacement current through the plates of the capacitor, would be, respectively

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Capacitance \( C = 20\ \mu\text{F} = 20 \times 10^{-6}\text{ F} \)
Rate of potential change \( \frac{dV}{dt} = 3\text{ V/s} \)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Conduction current \( I_c \) flows in the connecting wires while displacement current \( I_d \) exists in the dielectric region between capacitor plates.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Conduction current: \[ I_c = \frac{dq}{dt} = C \frac{dV}{dt} \]
By Maxwell's equation for current continuity: \[ I_d = I_c \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate conduction current \( I_c \): \[ I_c = (20 \times 10^{-6}\text{ F}) \times (3\text{ V/s}) = 60 \times 10^{-6}\text{ A} = 60\ \mu\text{A} \]
Since displacement current equals conduction current: \[ I_d = 60\ \mu\text{A} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The conduction current and displacement current are respectively \( 60\ \mu\text{A} \) and \( 60\ \mu\text{A} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q19 - Composition of alpha particle

questiontext.text: \( \alpha \)-particle consists of

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
An \( \alpha \)-particle is a doubly ionized helium nucleus, represented as \( \text{He}^{2+} \).

Evaluation
The helium nucleus \( {_2^4\text{He}} \) contains 2 protons (atomic number \( Z = 2 \)) and 2 neutrons (mass number minus atomic number \( A - Z = 4 - 2 = 2 \)). Because it is completely stripped of its 2 orbital electrons, an \( \alpha \)-particle contains zero electrons.

Final Conclusion
An \( \alpha \)-particle consists of 2 protons and 2 neutrons only.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q20 - Minimum angular velocity of rotating cylinder to hold block

questiontext.text: A block of mass 10 kg is in contact against the inner wall of a hollow cylindrical drum of radius 1 m. The coefficient of friction between the block and the inner wall of the cylinder is 0.1. The minimum angular velocity needed for the cylinder to keep the block stationary when the cylinder is vertical and rotating about its axis, will be (\( g = 10\text{ m/s}^2 \))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of block \( m = 10\text{ kg} \)
Radius of cylinder \( R = 1\text{ m} \)
Coefficient of static friction \( \mu = 0.1 \)
Acceleration due to gravity \( g = 10\text{ m/s}^2 \)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The drum rotates about its vertical axis. The normal force \( N \) exerted by the wall on the block provides the necessary centripetal force. Static friction \( f_s \) acts vertically upward balancing the downward gravitational weight.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Centripetal force: \[ N = m \omega^2 R \]
Vertical equilibrium condition: \[ f_s = mg \]
Maximum static friction limit: \[ f_s \le \mu N \implies mg \le \mu (m \omega^2 R) \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Solve for minimum angular velocity \( \omega_{\text{min}} \): \[ mg = \mu m \omega_{\text{min}}^2 R \implies \omega_{\text{min}} = \sqrt{\frac{g}{\mu R}} \]
Substitute numerical values: \[ \omega_{\text{min}} = \sqrt{\frac{10}{0.1 \times 1}} = \sqrt{100} = 10\text{ rad/s} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The minimum angular velocity needed to keep the block stationary is \( 10\text{ rad/s} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q21 - Effect of temperature increase on gas molecules

questiontext.text: Increase in temperature of a gas filled in a container would lead to

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
According to kinetic theory of gases, absolute temperature \( T \) is a direct measure of the average translational kinetic energy of gas molecules: \[ E_k = \frac{3}{2} k_B T \]

Evaluation
- As temperature increases, the mean root-square velocity of gas molecules increases, leading directly to an increase in kinetic energy.
- Increase in temperature increases pressure for a rigid container (\( P \propto T \)), does not change container volume or intermolecular distance, and does not alter mass.

Final Conclusion
An increase in temperature of a gas leads to an increase in its kinetic energy.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q22 - Induced emf in rotating coil in magnetic field

questiontext.text: A 800 turn coil of effective area \( 0.05\text{ m}^2 \) is kept perpendicular to a magnetic field \( 5 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T} \). When the plane of the coil is rotated by \( 90^\circ \) around any of its coplanar axis in \( 0.1\text{ s} \), the emf induced in the coil will be

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Number of turns \( N = 800 \)
Effective area \( A = 0.05\text{ m}^2 \)
Magnetic field \( B = 5 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T} \)
Rotation angle \( \Delta \theta = 90^\circ \)
Time interval \( \Delta t = 0.1\text{ s} \)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Initially, the normal to the plane of the coil is aligned with the magnetic field (\( \theta_1 = 0^\circ \)). After rotating by \( 90^\circ \), the normal is perpendicular to the field (\( \theta_2 = 90^\circ \)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Initial flux linkage: \[ \Phi_1 = N B A \cos(0^\circ) = N B A \]
Final flux linkage: \[ \Phi_2 = N B A \cos(90^\circ) = 0 \]
Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction (magnitude of induced emf): \[ e = \left| \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} \right| = \frac{\Phi_1 - \Phi_2}{\Delta t} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate initial flux: \[ \Phi_1 = 800 \times (5 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}) \times (0.05\text{ m}^2) = 2 \times 10^{-3}\text{ Wb} \]
Calculate induced emf magnitude: \[ e = \frac{2 \times 10^{-3}\text{ Wb}}{0.1\text{ s}} = 2 \times 10^{-2}\text{ V} = 0.02\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The induced emf in the coil is \( 0.02\text{ V} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q23 - Electric field midway between parallel infinite line charges

questiontext.text: Two parallel infinite line charges with linear charge densities \( +\lambda\text{ C/m} \) and \( -\lambda\text{ C/m} \) are placed at a distance of 2R in free space. What is the electric field mid-way between the two line charges?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Linear charge density of positive line charge = \( +\lambda \)
Linear charge density of negative line charge = \( -\lambda \)
Separation between lines = \( 2R \)
Distance of midpoint from each line = \( R \)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The lines are infinitely long and parallel in vacuum. Electric field points away from positive charge and towards negative charge.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Electric field due to an infinite line charge at distance \( R \): \[ E = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 R} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Electric field due to positive line charge at midpoint: \[ E_1 = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 R} \quad \text{(directed towards the negative line)} \]
Electric field due to negative line charge at midpoint: \[ E_2 = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 R} \quad \text{(directed towards the negative line)} \]
Since both electric fields point in the same direction, the total electric field magnitude is: \[ E_{\text{total}} = E_1 + E_2 = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 R} + \frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 R} = \frac{2\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 R} = \frac{\lambda}{\pi\varepsilon_0 R} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The electric field midway between the two line charges is \( \frac{\lambda}{\pi\varepsilon_0 R}\text{ N/C} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q24 - Angle of refraction at critical angle of incidence

questiontext.text: In total internal reflection when the angle of incidence is equal to the critical angle for the pair of media in contact, what will be angle of refraction?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
By Snell's Law, when light travels from a denser medium of refractive index \( n_1 \) to a rarer medium of refractive index \( n_2 \): \[ n_1 \sin(i) = n_2 \sin(r) \]

Evaluation
The critical angle \( i_c \) is defined specifically as the angle of incidence in the denser medium for which the angle of refraction in the rarer medium reaches \( 90^\circ \), causing the refracted light ray to graze along the boundary interface.

Final Conclusion
When the angle of incidence equals the critical angle, the angle of refraction is \( 90^\circ \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q25 - de Broglie wavelength of accelerated electron

questiontext.text: An electron is accelerated through a potential difference of 10,000 V. Its de-Broglie wavelength is (nearly): (\( m_e = 9 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg} \))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Accelerating potential difference \( V = 10,000\text{ V} = 10^4\text{ V} \)
Mass of electron \( m_e = 9 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg} \)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The electron starts from rest and gains kinetic energy \( K = eV \). Non-relativistic formulation applies since \( eV \ll m_e c^2 \).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
de-Broglie wavelength of an electron: \[ \lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m_e e V}} = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}\ \text{Å} = \frac{12.27 \times 10^{-10}}{\sqrt{V}}\text{ m} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute \( V = 10^4\text{ V} \): \[ \sqrt{V} = \sqrt{10^4} = 100 \]
Calculate wavelength: \[ \lambda = \frac{12.27}{100}\ \text{Å} = 0.1227\ \text{Å} = 0.1227 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} = 12.27 \times 10^{-12}\text{ m} \approx 12.2 \times 10^{-12}\text{ m} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The de-Broglie wavelength of the accelerated electron is nearly \( 12.2 \times 10^{-12}\text{ m} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q26 - Variation of magnetic field with distance for solid cylindrical conductor

questiontext.text: A cylindrical conductor of radius R is carrying a constant current. The plot of the magnitude of the magnetic field B with the distance \( d \) from the centre of the conductor, is correctly represented by the figure

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Solid long cylindrical conductor of radius \( R \), carrying a constant uniform current \( I \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Current density \( J = \frac{I}{\pi R^2} \) is uniform across the cross-section of the cylinder.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Ampere's Circuital Law: \[ \oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 I_{\text{enclosed}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
1. Inside the conductor (\( d \le R \)):
Current enclosed by Amperian loop of radius \( d \): \[ I_{\text{enclosed}} = I \left(\frac{\pi d^2}{\pi R^2}\right) = I \frac{d^2}{R^2} \]
Applying Ampere's Law: \[ B(2\pi d) = \mu_0 I \frac{d^2}{R^2} \implies B_{\text{in}} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi R^2} d \]
Thus, \( B_{\text{in}} \propto d \) (magnetic field increases linearly from zero at the axis to maximum at the surface \( d = R \)).

2. Outside the conductor (\( d \ge R \)):
Total current enclosed: \[ I_{\text{enclosed}} = I \]
Applying Ampere's Law: \[ B(2\pi d) = \mu_0 I \implies B_{\text{out}} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi d} \]
Thus, \( B_{\text{out}} \propto \frac{1}{d} \) (magnetic field decreases inversely with distance outside the cylinder).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The correct plot shows a linear rise of \( B \) from the origin up to distance \( R \), followed by a hyperbolic decay (\( 1/d \)) for distance greater than \( R \).

answer.text: A graph showing \( B \) increasing linearly with \( d \) for \( d \le R \) and decreasing inversely with \( d \) for \( d > R \)
A graph showing \( B \) remaining constant for \( d \le R \) and decreasing for \( d > R \)
A graph showing \( B \) zero for \( d \le R \) and increasing for \( d > R \)
A graph showing \( B \) decreasing linearly with distance \( d \)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q27 - Condition for rainbow observation

questiontext.text: Pick the wrong answer in the context with rainbow.

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
A rainbow is formed due to the dispersion, refraction, and internal reflection of sunlight by water droplets suspended in the atmosphere. To observe a rainbow, sunlight must strike the water drops from behind the observer so that the rays refract, reflect internally, and emerge back towards the observer's eyes.

Evaluation
- An observer can see a rainbow only when their back is facing the Sun, not when facing towards the Sun. Thus, the statement claiming an observer sees a rainbow facing the Sun is incorrect.
- A rainbow is indeed a combined optical effect of dispersion, refraction, and reflection.
- A secondary rainbow is formed when light rays undergo two internal reflections inside water droplets.
- Due to the double internal reflection, the order of colors in a secondary rainbow is reversed compared to a primary rainbow (violet outside, red inside).

Final Conclusion
The statement "An observer can see a rainbow when his front is towards the sun" is incorrect.

answer.text: An observer can see a rainbow when his front is towards the sun.
Rainbow is a combined effect of dispersion refraction and reflection of sunlight.
When the light rays undergo two internal reflections in a water drop, a secondary rainbow is formed.
The order of colours is reversed in the secondary rainbow.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q28 - Kinetic and potential energy of atomic electron

questiontext.text: The total energy of an electron in an atom in an orbit is \( -3.4\text{ eV} \). Its kinetic and potential energies are, respectively.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Total energy of electron \( E = -3.4\text{ eV} \)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Bohr's model of hydrogen-like atom applies, where potential energy is reference to zero at infinity.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Relationship between total energy \( E \), kinetic energy \( K \), and potential energy \( U \): \[ K = -E \] \[ U = 2E = -2K \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate Kinetic Energy: \[ K = -(-3.4\text{ eV}) = 3.4\text{ eV} \]
Calculate Potential Energy: \[ U = 2(-3.4\text{ eV}) = -6.8\text{ eV} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The kinetic energy is \( 3.4\text{ eV} \) and the potential energy is \( -6.8\text{ eV} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q29 - Amplitude of simple harmonic oscillation

questiontext.text: The displacement of a particle executing simple harmonic motion is given by \[ y = A_0 + A \sin \omega t + B \cos \omega t. \] Then the amplitude of its oscillation is given by

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Displacement equation: \( y = A_0 + A \sin \omega t + B \cos \omega t \)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
\( A_0 \) is a constant representing a shift in the mean (equilibrium) position.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Superposition of two perpendicular/orthogonal harmonic components of the same frequency: \[ A \sin \omega t + B \cos \omega t = \sqrt{A^2 + B^2} \sin(\omega t + \phi) \]
where \( \tan \phi = \frac{B}{A} \).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Rewrite displacement with respect to the shifted mean position \( y_0 = A_0 \): \[ y - A_0 = \sqrt{A^2 + B^2} \sin(\omega t + \phi) \]
The amplitude is the maximum displacement relative to the mean position \( y - A_0 \): \[ \text{Amplitude} = \sqrt{A^2 + B^2} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The amplitude of oscillation is \( \sqrt{A^2 + B^2} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q30 - Carrier and dopant characteristics of p-type semiconductor

questiontext.text: For a p-type semiconductor, which of the following statements is true?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
A p-type semiconductor is created by doping an intrinsic tetravalent semiconductor (such as Silicon or Germanium) with trivalent impurity atoms (such as Boron, Aluminium, or Gallium).

Evaluation
Each trivalent atom creates a deficit of one bonding electron, introducing a hole in the valence band. Consequently, holes become the majority charge carriers, while thermally generated electrons form the minority charge carriers.

Final Conclusion
In a p-type semiconductor, holes are the majority carriers and trivalent atoms are the dopants.

answer.text: Holes are the majority carriers and trivalent atoms are the dopants.
Holes are the majority carriers and pentavalent atoms are the dopants.
Electrons are the majority carriers and pentavalent atoms are the dopants.
Electrons are the majority carriers and trivalent atoms are the dopants.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q31 - Application of eddy currents in electrical devices

questiontext.text: In which of the following devices, the eddy current effect is not used?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
Eddy currents are loops of electrical current induced within bulk conductors by a changing magnetic field. They are intentionally utilized in applications relying on electromagnetic damping or induction heating.

Evaluation
- Magnetic braking in trains uses induced eddy currents to generate opposing magnetic drag.
- Induction furnaces use high-frequency eddy currents to generate intense heat for melting metals.
- Electromagnets experience eddy currents in their cores during AC operations.
- An electric heater generates thermal energy strictly by direct Joule heating (\( I^2 R \)) of a resistive wire element carrying electric current, without utilizing eddy currents.

Final Conclusion
The eddy current effect is not used in an electric heater.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q32 - Swimmer direction for shortest path across river

questiontext.text: The speed of a swimmer in still water is \( 20\text{ m/s} \). The speed of river water is \( 10\text{ m/s} \) and is flowing due east. If he is standing on the south bank and wishes to cross the river along the shortest path, the angle at which he should make his strokes w.r.t. north is given by

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Swimmer speed relative to still water \( v_s = 20\text{ m/s} \)
River flow velocity \( v_r = 10\text{ m/s} \) due East.
Swimmer starts from South bank wanting to reach North bank along the shortest path (straight across, due North).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Let East be along positive \( x \)-axis and North along positive \( y \)-axis. The swimmer heads at an angle \( \theta \) West of North.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
For the net velocity vector to point strictly North, the eastward component of swimmer's velocity must exactly cancel the river flow: \[ v_s \sin \theta = v_r \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute speed values into component equation: \[ 20 \sin \theta = 10 \implies \sin \theta = \frac{10}{20} = \frac{1}{2} \]
Solve for \( \theta \): \[ \theta = 30^\circ \]
Since the swimmer must head upstream into the river flow to compensate for eastward drift, the direction is \( 30^\circ \) West of North.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The required angle w.r.t. North is \( 30^\circ \) West.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2019_Q33 - Elastic potential energy stored in extended wire

questiontext.text: When a block of mass M is suspended by a long wire of length L, the length of the wire becomes \( (L + l) \). The elastic potential energy stored in the extended wire is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of suspended block = \( M \)
Original length of wire = \( L \)
Extended length = \( L + l \implies \text{Elongation} = l \)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The wire obeys Hooke's law within its elastic limit. Stretching force exerted by gravity = \( Mg \).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Elastic potential energy stored in a stretched wire: \[ U = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{Stretching Force} \times \text{Elongation} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute stretching force \( F = Mg \) and extension \( l \): \[ U = \frac{1}{2} Mgl \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The elastic potential energy stored in the extended wire is \( \frac{1}{2} Mgl \).
